rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” points to the preceding punishment of those who disbelieved God’s signs; the phrase means punishment follows servants’ sins.
rows.anchor: الآية، (ذلك) إشارة إلى ما تقدم من أخذ الله بالعذاب

rows.speaker: أكثر النحويين
rows.claim: Most grammarians say the nūn of yakun is deleted because its nasal sound resembles a weak letter and it occurs word-finally.
rows.anchor: أكثر النحويين يقولون: إنما حذفت النون لأنها تشبه بما فيها (¬4) من الغنة حروف اللين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general phonetic explanation fails to explain why nūn is also not deleted in forms such as yazin and yakhan.
rows.anchor: وهذا ينتقض بقولهم: لم يزن، ولم يخن

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى النحوي
rows.claim: Ali ibn Isa says kāna and yakūnu are the mother of verbs; their semantic centrality and frequent use allow a deletion unavailable to analogous verbs.
rows.anchor: وهذا تعليل ذكره علي بن عيسى النحوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author defers the full grammatical discussion to his treatment of Hud 11:109.
rows.anchor: وسنذكر تمام هذه المسألة في سورة هود عند قوله: {فلا تك في مرية مما يعبد هؤلاء} [هود: 109]

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: God fed Mecca after hunger, secured it from fear, and sent Muhammad as a messenger; these blessings would have remained had they not changed them through ingratitude and failure to give thanks, whereupon God removed them and punished them.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: إن الله تعالى أطعم أهل مكة من جوع وآمنهم من خوف وبعث إليهم محمدا رسولا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies God’s blessing as Muhammad, given to Quraysh; when they disbelieved and rejected him, God transferred him to the Anṣār.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: نعمة الله: محمد عليه السلام أنعم به على قريش فكفروا به وكذبوه فنقله إلى الأنصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By rejecting Muhammad and seeking to kill him, they changed the blessing; God then changed their worldly blessings and took them with afterlife punishment.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذا هم غيروا هذه النعمة عليهم بمحمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بتكذيبهم وقصدهم قتله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: God hears what they say and knows their intentions.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد: سميع لقولكم، عليم بنياتكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: “From among yourselves” means Muhammad; the Arab tribes shared in his ancestry through their Mudar, Rabiʿa, and Yemeni branches.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد: محمدا - صلى الله عليه وسلم -، وليس في العرب قبيلة إلا وقد ولدت النبي

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the phrase means he was from al-Muḥarrab of the descendants of Ishmael.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: من المحرب من بني إسماعيل

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the Messenger is a human like them, which makes the proof stronger because people understand someone like themselves; the author treats this at 3:164.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: أي: هو بشر مثلكم فهو أوكد للحجة عليكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Messenger finds their hardship and every harm that reaches them painful.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد: يعز عليه مشقتكم وكل مضرة تصيبكم

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: “Dear to him” means their hardship is severe for him because it is beyond his ability to remove; what burdens them is harm, and ʿanata describes severe distress with no apparent way out.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: معنى: {عزيز عليه} شديد عليه بامتناعه من إمكان زواله

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj paraphrases the phrase as “your hardship is severe for him,” meaning that you encounter difficulty and distress.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: معناه: عزيز عليه عنتكم، وهو لقاء الشدة والمشقة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ parses mā as nominative, meaning “your hardship is severe for him.”
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: (ما) في موضع رفع، معناه: عزيز عليه عنتكم

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق، الكلبي
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq and al-Kalbī understand him to be keen for your faith, with an omitted genitive complement.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: أي: حريص على إيمانكم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes the phrase to mean that the Messenger is eager for you to believe.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: حريص عليكم أن تؤمنوا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains ḥarīṣ as guarding you from entering the Fire: zeal for something means guarding it lest it be lost or destroyed.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: الحريص الشحيح بأن تدخلوا النار

rows.speaker: عطاء، ابن عباس
rows.claim: In a report from ʿAṭāʾ through Ibn ʿAbbās, God names the Messenger with two of His own names, raʾūf and raḥīm.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء، عن ابن عباس: سماه الله تعالى باسمين من أسمائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daʿwā is a verbal noun like duʿāʾ; the author points to the same word at 7:5.
rows.anchor: الدعوى: مصدر كالدعاء، ذكرنا ذلك في قوله: {فما كان دعواهم} [الأعراف: 5]

rows.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Whenever the people of Paradise desire something, they say the formula and receive it; after tasting it they praise God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية سعيد بن جبير: كلما اشتهى أهل الجنة شيئا قالوا: {سبحانك اللهم} فجاءهم ما يشتهون

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: When a desired bird passes, the people of Paradise say the formula and are given it; after satisfying their desire they praise God.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جرير: إذا مر بهم الطير يشتهونه قالوا: {سبحانك اللهم} فيؤتون به

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says “Glory be to You, O God” is a signal between the people of Paradise and their attendants, who bring what they desire when they hear it.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: قوله: {سبحانك اللهم} علم بين أهل الجنة والخدام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، الكلبي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Kalbī say the inhabitants greet one another with peace.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس والكلبي: يحيي بعضهم بعضا بالسلام

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others say the angels greet the people of Paradise and God greets them with peace; on this reading, the verbal noun is annexed to its object.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: تحية الملائكة إياهم، وتحية الله إياهم سلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the view that God and the angels greet them, taḥiyya is a verbal noun annexed to its object.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا أضيف المصدر إلى المفعول

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says that after one of them finishes speaking, he says, “Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.”
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: إذا فرغ أحدهم من كلامه (¬6) يقول: الحمد لله رب العالمين

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says that when they finish and drink, they praise God for what He has given them.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: إذا فرغوا وشربوا قالوا: الحمد لله على ما أعطاهم

rows.speaker: الحسن عن النبي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports from the Prophet that the people of Paradise are inspired to praise and glorify God as people are inspired to breathe.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن في هذه الآية عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq says they begin by magnifying and declaring God’s transcendence and end by thanking and praising Him.
rows.anchor: أبو إسحاق: أعلم الله -عز وجل- أنهم يبتدئون بتعظيم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An is the weakened form of inna and no longer governs because weakening removes its resemblance to a verb; the cited verse line illustrates an understood anna-hu.
rows.anchor: (أن) هي المخففة من الشديدة فلذلك لم تعمل لخروجها بالتخفيف عن شبه الفعل

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: The author of al-Naẓm holds that an here is an extra particle.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب النظم: (أن) هاهنا زائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command refers to God’s command to punish and destroy them.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: {حتى إذا جاء أمرنا} أي: أمرنا بعذابهم وإهلاكهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In the report through al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Ibn ʿAbbās says the tannūr sign was water appearing on the earth’s surface, at which Noah was told to board.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬1) في رواية الضحاك: ظهر الماء على وجه الأرض

rows.speaker: عكرمة، الزهري، ابن عيينة، الوالبي عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The same water-on-the-surface interpretation is attributed to ʿIkrima, al-Zuhrī, Ibn ʿUyayna, and another transmission from Ibn ʿAbbās through al-Wālibī.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول عكرمة والزهري وابن عيينة (¬2)، ورواية الوالبي أيضا عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda reports that the tannūr was the highest, most elevated part of the land and served as a sign between Noah and God.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة (¬4): ذكر لنا (¬5) أنه أرفع الأرض وأشرفها، جعل ذلك علامة بين نوح عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: On Qatāda’s view, water sprang from the upper and elevated places, likened to ovens because of their height.
rows.anchor: والمعنى على هذا: ونبع الماء من أعالي الأرض ومن الأمكنة المرتفعة، فشبهت لعلوها بالتنانير

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī says the tannūr means the dawn, so the sign was sunrise.
rows.anchor: روي عن علي (¬7) رضي الله عنه أنه قال: هو تنوير الصبح

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: On the dawn interpretation, light emerged as night ended; the succession of lights was likened to fire coming from an oven.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر: ومن ذهب إلى هذا قال: المعنى وبرز النور

rows.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية عطية وعطاء
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, in reports through ʿAṭiyya and ʿAṭāʾ, identifies the tannūr as the oven used for baking; Noah was told to board when water boiled from it.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس (¬1) في رواية عطية وعطاء: يريد التنور الذي يخبز فيه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the oven was made of stone and had passed from Adam and Eve to Noah.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن (¬2): وكان تنورا من حجارة، وكان لآدم وحواء

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
rows.claim: Muqātil ibn Sulaymān, citing several exegetes, locates Noah’s oven at ʿAyn Warda in Syria.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن سليمان (¬3) عن عدة من أهل التفسير: فار التنور من أقصى دار نوح بعين وردة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says water sprang from the oven, Noah’s wife saw and told him, and the oven was near Kufa.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد (¬4): نبع الماء من التنور فعلمت به امرأته فأخبرته، وكان ذلك بناحية الكوفة

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī shares the interpretation that the tannūr was the baker’s oven.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الشعبي (¬5) واختيار الفراء (¬6)

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ selects the literal baker’s oven interpretation.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الشعبي (¬5) واختيار الفراء (¬6)

rows.speaker: الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī, through Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās, also gives the baker’s oven interpretation.
rows.anchor: ونحو هذا قال الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abū Bakr prefers the ordinary bread oven because a literal, real meaning takes precedence over metaphor and analogy.
rows.anchor: القول الذي يذهب إليه: هو أن التنور تنور الخبز؛ # لأن الحمل على الظاهر

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth says tannūr is a word used generally in every language and calls its owner tannār.
rows.anchor: فقال الليث (¬3): التنور عمت بكل لسان وصاحبه تنار

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azharī infers that tannūr is a foreign word Arabized into the faʿūl pattern: its root is t-n-r, and Arabic has no nūn before rāʾ; Arab usage made loanwords Arabic.
rows.anchor: قال الأزهري: وهذا يدل على أن الاسم أعجمي فعربته العرب

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says two things are called a pair and cites 51:49, where God says He created all things in pairs.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الحسن الأخفش (¬6): يقال للاثنين هما زوجان

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan illustrates paired creation with heaven and earth, seasons, and night and day, ending with God alone, unlike anything.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن (¬7): السماء زوج، والأرض زوج، والشتاء زوج، والصيف زوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zawj can refer to a woman or to a man as husband; 4:1 calls the woman created from Adam his zawj.
rows.anchor: ويقال للمرأة هي # زوج، وللرجل (¬1) هو زوجها

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labīd’s verse uses zawj to mean two things, supporting the word’s use for an individual member of a pair.
rows.anchor: قال لبيد (¬3): زوج عليه كلة وقرامها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The livestock list in 6:143–144 shows zawj can designate one male or female in each pair; min kull zawjayni is generic for each kind of pair.
rows.anchor: ثمانية أزواج من الضأن اثنين ومن المعز اثنين قل آلذكرين حرم أم الأنثيين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، مجاهد، قتادة، الضحاك
rows.claim: They say Noah was to take each male and female pair aboard the ship.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬5) في قوله: {احمل فيها} يريد في السفينة

rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ reads min kullin with tanwīn, meaning “of everything”; a genitive complement is omitted and ithnayn is an emphatic adjective of zawjayni, as in 16:51.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حفص (¬3) {من كل} بالتنوين أراد من كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the common reading, ithnayn is accusative through the verb of carrying rather than an adjective describing zawjayni.
rows.anchor: وعلى قراءة العامة نصب اثنين بالحمل، وليس صفة لزوجين

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Ahlak means Noah’s children and household; he was to carry the believers, excluding those already decreed to drown for their deeds and disbelief, namely his wife Wāʿila and son Kanʿān.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون (¬6): يعني ولده وعياله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says eighty people believed with Noah, including his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth and three daughters-in-law.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬8): ثمانون إنسانا وكان فيهم ثلاثة من بنيه: سام وحام ويافث

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان وغيره
rows.claim: Muqātil and other authorities give the same report of eighty believers with Noah.
rows.anchor: ونحو ذلك قال مقاتل بن سليمان (¬1) وغيره

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان وغيره
rows.claim: They say the Village of Eighty near Mosul was named for the survivors who settled there after leaving the ark; eighty is called few relative to Noah’s nation.
rows.anchor: وقالوا: قرية الثمانين (¬2) بناحية الموصل، إنما سميت لأن هؤلاء لما خرجوا من السفينة

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq explains that eighty is few compared with the whole nation of Noah.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: لأن ثمانين (¬3) قليل في جملة أمة نوح

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī explains singular qalīl as a form built for plural reference, so it needs no plural marker; 26:54 adds one for assurance, like the plural word buyūtāt.
rows.anchor: ووحد القليل؛ لأنه لفظ مبني للجمع لما كان الواحد لا يوصف (¬4) به ولا الاثنين

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī offers another parse: a plural described by a singular form, understood as “only a few people believed with him.”
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يقال في توحيد القليل إنه وصف لجمع خرج على تقطيع الواحد

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: He also allows that a plural is intended and one singular form suffices, citing poetry where a collective is expressed with singular jild.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد الجمع فاكتفى بالواحد منه، كقوله (¬5): قد عض أعناقهم جلد الجواميس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah tells those he ordered to board to ride; rakiba broadly means to mount or rise onto something, including an animal, ship, land, or sea, and also occurs in the expression for debt burdening someone.
rows.anchor: الركوب العلو على ظهر الشيء، فمنه ركوب الدابة، وركوب السفينة، وركوب البر، وركوب البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs call passengers on a ship rukāb al-safīna, whereas rukbān, arkūb, and rukb refer to riders of animals and camels.
rows.anchor: وتسمي العرب من يركب السفينة ركاب السفينة

rows.speaker: ابن أحمر
rows.claim: Ibn Aḥmar calls ship passengers rukbānan in a poem, supporting the broader usage for seafarers.
rows.anchor: وقد جعل ابن أحمر ركاب السفينة ركبانا فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fī cannot depend on the verb rukūb because Arabic says “I rode the ship,” not “I rode in the ship”; the object is omitted, understood as water, and fīhā is circumstantial.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز أن تكون (في) من صلة الركوب؛ لأنه يقال: ركبت السفينة، ولا يقال: ركبت في السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the meaning is “board it,” with fī as an emphatic addition; it directs them to the ark’s interior, since simply saying “board it” might suggest its deck.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يقال المعنى: اركبوها أي الفلك، وزاد (في) للتأكيد كقوله: {للرؤيا تعبرون} [يوسف: 43]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Majrā is a verbal noun like ijrāʾ; compare “a blessed landing” and the verbal nouns madkhal and makhraj at 17:80.
rows.anchor: المجرى: مصدر كالإجراء، ومثله قوله: {منزلا مباركا}

rows.speaker: صاحب هذه القراءة
rows.claim: The reading majrāhā with an open mīm is also a verbal noun like jary; its advocate cites the ship’s running with them in waves in 11:42.
rows.anchor: وقرئ {مجراها} (¬3) بفتح الميم وهو أيضا مصدر مثل الجري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marsā is a verbal noun from arsā, to become fixed or to make something fixed; 79:32 says God fixed the mountains.
rows.anchor: وأما المرسى: فهو أيضا مصدر كالإرساء يقال: وما الشيء يرسو: إذا ثبت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, through ʿAṭāʾ, says the ship runs by God’s name and power.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬5) في رواية عطاء: يريد تجرى باسم الله وقدرته

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says Noah said “In God’s name” when he wanted the ship to sail, and again when he wanted it to settle.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك (¬6): كان إذا أراد أن تجري قال: باسم الله فجرت

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the ship sails by God and settles by Him; bismillāh here means “by God,” so the reported explanations share one meaning.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق (¬2): أي بالله تجري وبه تستقر، ومعنى قولنا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ offers two parses: majrāhā and marsāhā may be raised by the preposition bi, or bismillāh can stand alone while both nouns are accusative as adverbials of running and settling.
rows.anchor: فقال الفراء (¬3): إن شئت جعلت (مجراها) و (مرساها) في موضع رفع بالباء

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī explains the first parse: bi is grammatically the predicate and raises the subject, while its sense is accusative, “its running occurs by God’s name.”
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أن يرتفع المجرى بالباء الزائدة، وتفتقر الباء إلى المجرى؛ لأنها خبره ورافعته

rows.speaker: الفراء، ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: The second of al-Farrāʾ and Ibn al-Anbārī’s parses makes majrāhā accusative as a time or place expression: “in its running and settling,” with the preposition omitted.
rows.anchor: القول الثاني: أن يكون المجرى في موضع نصب على مذهب الوقت # ومنهاج المحل

rows.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
rows.claim: Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā supplies an omitted verb for bi; it governs majrāhā, as in “its running and settling take place by God’s name.”
rows.anchor: وقال أحمد بن يحيى: الباء منصوبة بفعل محذوف يدل عليه ويكنى (¬2) منه

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī reads bismillāh as a circumstantial phrase for the riders, who board blessed by God’s name; compare the expression at 5:61.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي (¬3): قوله تعالى: {بسم الله} يجوز أن يكون حالا من الضمير

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: On his reading, majrāhā and marsāhā are temporal adverbials for the two inevitable periods of sailing and mooring, not times when they are commanded to board.
rows.anchor: ولا يكون الظرف متعلقا باركبوا؛ لأن المعنى ليس (¬4) عليه، ألا ترى أنه لا يراد اركبوا فيها في وقت الجري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī’s circumstantial parse is a separate interpretation from the explanations attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk.
rows.anchor: وهذا الوجه الذي ذكره أبو علي وجه آخر في التفسير سوى ما ذكرنا عن ابن عباس والضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God is forgiving toward the people in the ark and merciful to them.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬2): يريد غفور لأصحاب السفينة رحيم بهم

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The mention of forgiveness and mercy coheres with rescue by boarding: those blessings are obtained through obedience just as rescue was obtained.
rows.anchor: لأنه لما ذكرت النجاة بالركوب في السفينة، ذكرت النعمة بالمغفرة والرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawj is the plural of mawja, a great section rising from the body of water, especially when wind strengthens and the sea churns.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: {وهي تجري بهم} [هود: 42] أي الفلك {في موج} جمع موجة

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq says Noah’s son was an unbeliever named Yām.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق (¬5): كان كافرا واسمه يام

rows.speaker: الكلبي، مقاتل
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil say Noah’s son was named Kanʿān.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي ومقاتل (¬6): اسمه كنعان

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق، ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq and Ibn al-Anbārī say the son was apart from Noah’s religion because he was an unbeliever, though they also allow that he was apart from the ark.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق (¬7) وابن الأنباري: أي من دين نوح؛ لأنه كان كافرا مخالفا عن نوح

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abū Bakr prefers that the son was physically separated from the ark.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر: وهذا أشبه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Moses’s signs refer to the Torah and the obligations and rulings God revealed in it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬2): يريد التوراة وما أنزل الله فيها من الفرائض والأحكام

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the signs are proofs that establish the truth of Moses’s prophethood.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬3): أي بعلاماتنا التي تدل على صحة نبوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A manifest authority is a clear proof that overcomes the opposing claim and is free of confusion and deception.
rows.anchor: حجة بينة وبرهان يتسلط به على إبطال قول من خالفه، مخلص من التلبيس والتمويه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the manifest authority as Moses’s staff, which God made a punishment and scourge no creature could withstand.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬4): يعني عصاه التي جعل الله فيها عذابا ونقمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh ordered the people to worship him and take him as a deity, and they followed that command; his command did not guide them to good.
rows.anchor: أي أمرهم بعبادته واتخاذه إلها فاتبعوا ما أمرهم به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Pharaoh did not guide his people or his followers.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬5): يريد لم يرشد قومه ولا من اتبعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaqdumu means he leads them; fa-awradahum means he brought them into the Fire. The past tense presents the certain future as already completed.
rows.anchor: أنه (¬7) يقدمهم إلى النار، يدل على هذا قوله: {فأوردهم النار}

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj adds qadūman as a verbal form and says yaqdam, aqdama, and istaqdama have the same meaning.
rows.anchor: وزاد الزجاج (¬6): قدوما، ويقدم وأقدم واستقدم بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās compares Pharaoh’s leading his people into the Fire with his leading them into the sea in worldly life, where he drowned them.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد كما تقدم قومه في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author glosses biʾsa here as “the Fire.”
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {وبئس} أي النار

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abū Bakr explains the masculine and feminine forms of biʾsa/niʿma by agreement with the implied word manzil or the feminine dār.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر (¬2): وذكر (بئس النار) لتذكير الورد كما تقول: نعم المنزل دارك

rows.speaker: الكلبي، مقاتل، المفسرون
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī, Muqātil, and the exegetes gloss al-wird al-mawrūd as an entrance that is entered.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي (¬5) ومقاتل (¬6) والمفسرون (¬7): المدخل المدخول

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sikkīt says wird can mean people’s arrival at water, the water approached, or the camels arriving to drink.
rows.anchor: قال ابن السكيت (¬8): الورد ورود القوم الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this lexical reading, wird can be a verbal noun meaning arrival, or the place or thing one approaches; here it is the destination, in a passive sense.
rows.anchor: والذي في هذه الآية يراد به الموضع الذي يورد، وهو بمعنى المفعول

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The cited poem describes camels expected to reach water at midday but arriving at night because of their strength and energy, illustrating wird as arrival.
rows.anchor: إذا القوم قالوا وردهن ضحى غدا ... تواهفن حتى وردهن طروق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wird can also denote those arriving, as in 19:86, where the criminals are driven to Hell as entrants; a verbal noun may be named for its agent or object.
rows.anchor: كقوله: {ونسوق المجرمين إلى جهنم وردا} [مريم: 86] أي واردين

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says Arabs use the verbal noun wird for the destination reached; here the meaning is that the destination to which they are brought is an evil one: the Fire.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري (¬3): الورد مصدر معناه: الورود تجعله العرب بمعنى الموضع المورود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers learn from the destruction of nations who rejected their prophets; the stories soften hearts toward truth and recall the good, evil, and consequences shown in the fates of disbelievers and believers.
rows.anchor: يريد أنهم يتعظون إذا سمعوا هذه السورة بما نزل بالأمم لما كذبوا أنبياءهم

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj reads the command to wait as a threat: they may wait for Satan’s promised outcome, while believers await God’s promised victory and ascendancy.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says the unbelievers are to await the punishment that will befall them.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق (¬2) {وانتظروا} ما يحل بكم من العذاب

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī parses ghayb as a verbal noun annexed to its object after omission of a preposition, and allows either all hidden intelligent beings or God’s knowledge of the unseen; 6:73 supports the latter.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي (¬3): الغيب مصدر مضاف إلى المفعول على الاتساع وحذف حرف الجر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية الوالبي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, in al-Wālibī’s transmission, says the phrase means the treasuries of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬6) في رواية الوالبي: يعني خزائن السموات والأرض

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says it means everything hidden from people.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك (¬7): يعني جميع ما غاب عن العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the resurrection, all authority returns to God, leaving creatures without the worldly powers held by jurists and rulers.
rows.anchor: في المعاد حتى لا يكون # للخلق أمركما يكون في الدنيا للفقهاء والأمراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reading is cited and discussed at the author’s treatment of 2:210.
rows.anchor: وقرئ {يرجع} (¬1)، وذكرنا هذا مستقصى في المعنى والتوجيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not unaware because He repays the virtuous for their good deeds and the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: أي أنه يجزي المحسن بإحسانه والمسيء بإساءته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading yaʿmalūn in the third person refers generally to all people, believers and unbelievers.
rows.anchor: والمعنى في قوله: {يعملون} ينصرف إلى جميع الناس مؤمنهم وكافرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second-person reading taʿmalūn means the Prophet is told to address them directly.
rows.anchor: وقرئ (¬3) (تعملون) بالتاء على معنى قل لهم:
